newsitem.title: PANAMA: Noriegas sentenced in Panama for illegal enrichment.
newsitem.headline: Noriegas sentenced in Panama for illegal enrichment.

text.p: Panama's former strongman Manuel Antonio Noriega, his wife and three daughters were sentenced by a Fourth Circuit Supreme Court judge for amassing more than $15 million, officials said on Monday.

Noriega, serving a 40-year sentence in Florida for his 1992 conviction on drug and racketeering charges, was sentenced to 18 months for amassing more than $8 million from 1986 until his capture by U.S. troops in December 1989, a Supreme Court spokesman told Reuters.

Judge Sandra Lorena y Thays also sentenced Noriega's wife, Felizidad Sieiro de Noriega, to 18 months and three daughters Thaise, Lorena and Sandra, to 12 months each, the spokesman said. Noriega's wife and three daughters do not live in Panama.
The sentence was handed down last week but was not made public until Monday, the spokesman said.
Noriega was charged with illegally amassing properties worth $3 million and bank accounts of more than $4 million. His daughters allegedly obtained apartments and businesses worth $680,000.
The Supreme Court spokesman could not say whether the bank accounts and properties were in Panama or elsewhere.
